newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar slumps to end at three-week low.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar slumps to end at three-week low.

text.p: Heavy fund selling pummeled CSCE world sugar prices Thursday, dragging the market to its lowest close in three weeks despite a late round of bargain hunting by the trade, market sources said.

In its fourth consecutive negative close, commodity funds scrambled to liquidate long positions acquired during last week's rally above 11.00 cents a lb. The selling pressure accelerated toward midsession, as sell stops were triggered in the 10.72-10.70 range in March delivery.
Selling by the funds drove March to a low of 10.61 before trade buying and some last-minute shortcovering by locals recouped some of the losses.

"Once we got to the lows, the trade was anxious to buy," said one dealer, noting the market had fallen some 50 points since the high reached on Monday. "But it couldn't get too far to the upside because the specs were selling."
March futures finished down 0.15 cent at 10.72 cents after trading from 10.61 to 10.84. May delivery slipped 0.11 cent to 10.83, with the rest off 0.09 to 0.10.
The nearby switches were well offered throughout the day, adding to the overall bearish tone, dealers said.
On the charts, traders pegged 10.57 cents as the next key support level. March would need to break above 10.85-10.90 to shore up its stance, with major resistance seen toward 11.00 cents.
Volume was estimated at a heavy 28,859 lots.
